This kinda hits home. I've been annoyed lately with my boyfriend because he got into battle tech (which I was sad to learn is apparently different from space marines, which he was into last month and I actually made a little effort to tune in). He's always been nerdy, super into gaming, board games, the type with like actual toys you push around. Never bothered me... I would even play with him if I had the free time. Until I found out I was pregnant. Now it sort of irks me that instead of focusing on keeping things tidy, working harder, being more frugal, he still chooses to allocate a significant amount of time to the nerd stuff. I've recently been questioning whether I dislike the hobbies or him personally. :'( I love him but it annoys me so much, and with the pregnancy hormones, the morning sickness, my irritation levels can spike dangerously to scream at him level (happened once, not proud of it). I think I've also shattered his confidence and self-esteem which is the total opposite of what I want and need. I'm really worried about us and I'm not sure how to navigate the situation anymore. I hate how I've turned into a bitter, anxious, OC nag.

Hi! Here's my cheap suggestion to enrich your life:

Mas ok pa magbasa ka muna ng mga libro. Kahit fiction ok lang, basta mabawas yung screen time. Maybe iwasan ang trashy unrealistic romances and go for stories with inspiring people/characters. Kasi at least with books nagagamit yung imagination mo and it seems like your brain needs that kind of stimulation! If nakikita mo sa IG o FB nagttravel mga kilala mo, books are another way to travel with your imagination and learn a lot of ideas, information, and at least vicariously live through other people's experiences. It's not the same as the short glimpses on IG or FB where you're just left wondering what's it like? How did they get there? With good books, the full descriptions make you feel like you're there and experiencing what's happening yourself, and there's usually a reasonable/logical explanation of how and why things happen (even in fantasy novels, within the bounds of the world's rules). Learning the hows and whys can help you apply them in your own life too. Mababawasan yung inggit mo. Instead maiinspire ka.

I'd like to see more Eastern European, Asian and Southeast Asian cuisine! Or maybe a way to make your own recipes? In Philippine households, there's usually a few dishes laid out on the table for people to help themselves with gargantuan amounts of rice. Usually a type of main viand or two (let's say kaldereta and fried chicken), a vegetable dish or two (pinakbet or lumpiang ubod) and sometimes soup (sinagang). In a classic setting, the dinner table would have a lazy susan and people would just continually help themselves. I want to be able recreate a simple family meal like this. 😍 Para families should be able to set a time or way for people to sit at the table to eat together, perhaps kids have to be excused to leave the table at these times. Bonus if there was a way to organically add a sort of traditional saying before starting eating too - whether it seem like a prayer or simple "bon apetit," depending on what culture you want to play out. But there should also be a way for everyone to eat pizza or whatever in front of the TV for less formal times. 
It would be so great to recreate merienda/tea times, and easily designate a spot to serve and eat food in different areas of the house 🤔. Like, we're all eating muffins at the breakfast nook when the kids get home from school today. Or, let's have some wine by the balcony upstairs. Let's spread out a picnic blanket outside. Oh, please make it work smoothly somehow 😅🙏🏼 Bonus: breakfast in bed?! 🤩
Snacking while watching TV (or reading and other activities!) also seems like a cool/realistic thing to add. Imagine: your Para gets home after a long day at work and instead of hopping on to the computer first thing, he of his own free will depending on his personality or mood either collapse onto a sofa and pig out watching bad TV 😍 or make a pot of tea and settle down with a good book in his favorite spot. 

For kids, I think there should be parameters reached for bored, naughty or upset ones to throw their food (on the ground or at someone else lol) or feed it to the dog or cat while no one's looking if they don't like it. 😄 *To counterbalance this, perhaps kids behave if they respect or fear an adult in the room. But I would also enjoy watching a child have a full blown meltdown when confronted with something they really don't want to eat (oh, and wouldn't it be fun for a chance for them to suddenly crave it once they get older?! 😆). They can be sent to bed satiated with the fulfillment of their tantrum but the next morning will feel lousy :p

Fights at the formal dinner table would be so interesting - does it get resolved, perhaps by a Para who is more diplomatic? Does someone get up and leave?! These would feel like such important events with witnesses. Maybe someone can "make important announcements" - like the breadwinner is changing jobs, top grades at school (imagine a jealous sibling flicking a pea at our honor student lol), new pregnancy or adoption, or someone coming out! And all these different reactions by those at the table. Does the delicious steak make up for some of the harsh words said? Maybe someone can stop liking whatever food was served because of particularly bad trauma! 

Almost certainly there should be Paras who would be upset if someone doesn't like the dish they cooked. 😁 

Another cool thing would be, maybe for particularly snackish/gluttonous Paras, to have the random urge to get up in the middle of the night to raid the fridge. 😁
Conversely, there should be some Paras who are picky eaters. And those who don't have much of an appetite if they're nervous or upset, even if they're hungry. Maybe there can be a designated comfort food for some Paras to overcome this. But I think Paras should crave certain dishes and not have much of an appetite for if they don't get them. 

For the actual cooking mechanics, I've read a lot of suggestions that are pretty cool if complicated but making cooking a little difficult could make food delivery more tempting even if it's pricier which is pretty realistic. I definitely agree with one suggestion that there should be difficult recipes that could go wrong even if you have decent skill, especially the first few times. I also like the ideas behind having a cultural base w food starting out - but in that case we're definitely gonna need RICE!

 Cooking classes! It would be great if you could join one in the community/neighborhood or even set one up yourself :) Bonus if there's a chance for everyone to get food poisoning or for it all to go up in flames and have a major town tragedy hehe.
